Christmas Spectacular Starring The Radio City Rockettes

11:00 AM · Radio City Music Hall, Midtown-Times Square · ↻ Every Wednesday

Children younger than 24 months may attend without the purchase of a ticket, however, they may not occupy their own separate seat and must sit on a parent or guardian's lap. Please note that government mandates, venue protocols and event requirements are subject to change. Be sure to visit rockettes.com/faq for the latest information. There is a fourteen (14) ticket limit per purchaser over the entire 2026 Christmas Spectacular season. The Christmas Spectacular is an immersive experience that includes confetti, pyrotechnics, smoke effects, intense lighting, visual effects, loud noises, flashing lights and flying objects (drones). Such elements may aggravate certain medical or physical conditions, and guests should take into consideration if they have a history of discomfort or physical symptoms when experiencing these elements.

A Ghost in Your Ear

7:00 PM · Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre, Greenwich Village · ↻ Every Wednesday Going out

When an actor arrives late to a sound studio for a last-minute audiobook recording session, he is handed the script of a chilling ghost story to read. But as the engineer cues the recording and the evening wears on, the horrors slowly begin to escape the page to haunt the studio itself. Fresh from an acclaimed, sold-out run in London, A GHOST IN YOUR EAR is the "truly terrifying headphone horror" (The Guardian) from the darkly brilliant mind of Tony Award® nominee Jamie Armitage (SIX), made in collaboration with Ben and Max Ringham (ANNA, National Theatre). A mesmerizing blend of gothic horror and psychological thriller, this cutting-edge theatrical experience uses groundbreaking binaural sound technology to immerse every audience member in a haunting world of sound. And at Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre - one of New York's most intimate venues - there's no escaping the frights. Enter if you dare.

Maria Schneider Orchestra

7:00 PM · Birdland Jazz Club, Hell's Kitchen · $45.76 Something special

Maria Schneiders music has been hailed by critics as evocative, majestic, magical, heart-stoppingly gorgeous, and beyond categorization. She and her 18-member orchestra have performed at concert halls around the world and have received 7 GRAMMYs, many Jazz Journalist Awards, and numerous DOWNBEAT and JAZZTIMES Readers and Critics Polls. Schneiders music blurs the lines between genres, making her long list of commissioners quite varied, stretching from jazz to classical, and dance, even collaborating with David Bowie. She is among a small few to have received GRAMMYs in multiple genres, having received the award in both jazz and classical, as well as for her work with David Bowie. Shes holds honorary doctorates from the University of Minnesota and Eastman School of Music. In 2019, the National Endowment for the Arts bestowed on Schneider the nations highest honor in jazz, naming her an NEA Jazz Master.

Pitch & Pair

7:30 PM · Brooklyn Improv (The Main Room), Williamsburg · $31.56 Singles

Got a single friend who's a total catch? It's time to play matchmaker with a twist! Create a slide deck presentation that showcases their best qualities, quirks, and charm. Then, take the stage and deliver a 3-5 minute pitch to a room full of eligible singles ready to mingle. Who knows? You might just spark the next great love story! Only Pitch tickets include a pitch spot - Attendance tickets are for watching only. Pitch tickets are only accessed and sold from the pitch request process. How It Works Tickets: Buy your tickets early to reserve your seat. Join the waitlist to purchase a pitch spot. (Request to pitch here) Presentations: Present your friend or sit back, sip your drink, and enjoy the presentations. After each presentation: There will be a Q&A session, and presenters will share their friends contact info (e.g., Instagram handle) on the last slide so audience members can slide into their DMs Mingle: After the pitches, you can mingle and make connections with anyone who caught your eye! This event will be filmed. By attending, you consent to being filmed and photographed by Joerky LLC d/b/a Pitch and Pair. Please review our filming release at https://www.pitchandpairnyc.com/filming-release for full details. Juilliard at The Apollo: Filles de Kilimanjaro

7:30 PM · The Apollo's Victoria Theater 1, Harlem (South) Going out

With a career defined by constant reinvention, Miles Davis continuously shaped and reshaped the sound of jazz, moving from bebop to cool jazz, post-bop to fusion, and beyond. His time in New York City, a hub of jazz innovation and culture, started with Juilliard. To mark the iconic alum's 100th birthday, Juilliard Jazz and the Apollo Theater present a series of multidisciplinary performances on the legendary Harlem stage, honoring some of Davis' landmark albums: Birth of the Cool, Bitches Brew, and Kind of Blue.

The Conversation

8:00 PM · Astor Place Theatre, Greenwich Village Going out

THE CONVERSATION follows Marcus (Tony Award-winner Joshua Henry) and Elle (Julia Harriman) from the electric spark of their first date to move-ins, milestones, and the slow accumulation of everything left unsaid. The score, written by Henry and Harriman, weaves soul, R&B, and modern pop into bold musical theater storytelling that is intimate, honest, and emotionally gripping. With a book by Nick Green and directed by Tony Award-winner Kenny Leon, The Conversation asks what it takes to choose love, even when it hurts, and what it takes to stay.
